title: What is good: error type design across the workspace
description:
The workspace's error type discipline is genuinely well-done and worth defending:

1. Every public error enum is #[non_exhaustive] with structured fields (not String messages). Callers can programmatically match on variants without parsing text.

2. DerError is an opaque newtype wrapping der::Error — insulating callers from upstream semver churn while preserving Display diagnostics. This is a hard pattern to get right (most Rust crypto crates expose der::Error directly and break on version bumps).

3. The Cow<'static, str> pattern for fixed-string error details (pkix-chain's ProfileViolation, OcspDelegation) preserves zero-allocation for the common case while supporting serde Deserialize (which needs Cow::Owned) without leaking memory.

4. Cache-friendly result types: the workspace non-negotiable #6 is enforced with compile-time Send+Sync assertions in pkix-revocation, pkix-chain, and pkix-truststore. Error types derive Clone+PartialEq+Eq throughout. IoFailure in pkix-truststore cleanly solves the 'io::Error is not Clone' problem without losing kind information.

5. Error::source() chains are consistently implemented, preserving the std::error::Error causal chain for every wrapping layer.

Locations: pkix-path/src/lib.rs (DerError), pkix-revocation/src/lib.rs (Error, OutOfScopeReason), pkix-chain/src/lib.rs (Error with From impls), pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs (Error, IoFailure), pkix-ct/src/lib.rs (Error), pkix-identity/src/lib.rs (IdentityError).
